text: The number of real roots of the equation $\sqrt{x^{2}-4x+3}+\sqrt{x^{2}-9}=\sqrt{4x^{2}-14x+6}$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Factorise: $x^{2}-4x+3=(x-1)(x-3)$, $x^{2}-9=(x-3)(x+3)$ and $4x^{2}-14x+6=(x-3)(4x-2)$.

All three radicands are non-negative only for $x\leq -3$ or $x\geq 3$.

At $x=3$ every term is 0, so $x=3$ is a root.

For $x>3$, dividing by $\sqrt{x-3}$: $\sqrt{x-1}+\sqrt{x+3}=\sqrt{4x-2}$. Squaring, $2x+2+2\sqrt{(x-1)(x+3)}=4x-2\Rightarrow \sqrt{x^{2}+2x-3}=x-2\Rightarrow x^{2}+2x-3=x^{2}-4x+4\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7}{6}$, which is not greater than 3.

For $x\leq -3$, dividing by $\sqrt{3-x}$: $\sqrt{1-x}+\sqrt{-x-3}=\sqrt{2-4x}$. Squaring, $-2x-2+2\sqrt{(1-x)(-x-3)}=2-4x\Rightarrow \sqrt{x^{2}+2x-3}=2-x\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7}{6}$, which is not $\leq -3$.

So $x=3$ is the only real root.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: A bag contains 6 balls. Two balls are drawn from it at random and both are found to be black. The probability that the bag contains at least 5 black balls is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $E_{i}\to$ Bag have at least $i$ black balls 

$E\to 2$ balls are drawn & both black

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore P\left (\dfrac{E_{5}\text{or}E_{6}}{E}\right )=\dfrac{P\left (\frac{E}{E_{5}}\right )+P\left (\frac{E}{E_{6}}\right )}{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{6}P\left (\frac{E}{E_{i}}\right )} \\  \\ =\dfrac{\frac{{}^{5}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}+\frac{{}^{6}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}}{0+\frac{{}^{2}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}+\frac{{}^{3}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}+\frac{{}^{4}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}+\frac{{}^{5}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}+\frac{{}^{6}C_{2}}{{}^{6}C_{2}}} \\  \\ =\dfrac{10+15}{1+3+6+10+15}=\dfrac{25}{35}=\dfrac{5}{7} \end{array}$

text: If $\sin ^{-1}\frac{α}{17}+\cos ^{-1}\frac{4}{5}-\tan ^{-1}\frac{77}{36}=0,0<α<13$, then $\sin ^{-1}(\sin α)+\cos ^{-1}(\cos α)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{α}{17}\right )=-\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{4}{5}\right )+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{77}{36}\right )$

Let $\cos ^{-1}\left (\frac{4}{5}\right )=p$ and $\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{77}{36}\right )=q$

$\Rightarrow \sin \left (\sin ^{-1}\frac{α}{17}\right )=\sin (q-p)$

$=\sin q\cdot \cos p-\cos q\cdot \sin p$

$\Rightarrow \frac{α}{17}=\frac{77}{85}\cdot \frac{4}{5}-\frac{36}{85}\cdot \frac{3}{5}$

$\Rightarrow α=\frac{200}{25}=8$

$\sin ^{-1}\sin 8+\cos ^{-1}\cos 8$

$=-8+3π+8-2π$

$=π$

text: If the sum and product of four positive consecutive terms of a G.P., are 126 and 1296 , respectively, then the sum of common ratios of all such GPs is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the terms be $a,ar,ar^{2},ar^{3}$ with $a,r>0$.

Product: $a^{4}r^{6}=1296\Rightarrow a^{2}r^{3}=36\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{6}{r^{3/2}}$.

Sum: $a\left (1+r+r^{2}+r^{3}\right )=126\Rightarrow \dfrac{1+r+r^{2}+r^{3}}{r^{3/2}}=21\Rightarrow \left (r^{3/2}+r^{-3/2}\right )+\left (r^{1/2}+r^{-1/2}\right )=21$.

Let $t=\sqrt{r}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r}}$, so $t\geq 2$ and $r^{3/2}+r^{-3/2}=t^{3}-3t$. Then

$t^{3}-3t+t=21\Rightarrow t^{3}-2t-21=0\Rightarrow (t-3)\left (t^{2}+3t+7\right )=0.$

The factor $t^{2}+3t+7$ has discriminant $9-28<0$, so the only real root is $t=3$.

$\sqrt{r}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r}}=3\Rightarrow r+1=3\sqrt{r}\Rightarrow r^{2}+2r+1=9r\Rightarrow r^{2}-7r+1=0.$

Both roots $r=\dfrac{7\pm 3\sqrt{5}}{2}$ are positive, so each gives a valid G.P., and the sum of the common ratios is $7$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
For the system of linear equations

$x+y+z=6$

$αx+βy+7z=3$

$x+2y+3z=14$

which of the following is NOT true ?
options: If $α=β=7$, then the system has no solution
For every point $(α,β)\neq (7,7)$ on the line $x-2y+7=0$, the system has infinitely many solutions
There is a unique point $(α,β)$ on the line $x+2y+18=0$ for which the system has infinitely many solutions
If $α=β$ and $α\neq 7$, then the system has a unique solution
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The coefficient determinant is

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ α & β & 7 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=(3β-14)-(3α-7)+(2α-β)=2β-α-7,$

so $\Delta =0$ exactly when $(α,β)$ lies on the line $x-2y+7=0$.

The first and third equations give $y+2z=8$, so their common solutions are $x=t-2,y=8-2t,z=t$. Substituting in the second equation gives

$(α-2β+7)t+(8β-2α)=3.$

For $α=β=7$ the second equation becomes $x+y+z=\dfrac{3}{7}$, which contradicts $x+y+z=6$, so there is no solution and (A) is true.

For $α=β\neq 7$, $\Delta =α-7\neq 0$, so the solution is unique and (D) is true.

On the line $α-2β+7=0$ the $t$ term vanishes, so there are infinitely many solutions only if $8β-2α=3$. With $α=2β-7$ this gives $4β+14=3$, so $β=-\dfrac{11}{4}$ and $α=-\dfrac{25}{2}$; every other point of that line gives no solution, so (B) is false.

The point $\left (-\dfrac{25}{2},-\dfrac{11}{4}\right )$ satisfies $-\dfrac{25}{2}-\dfrac{11}{2}+18=0$, so it lies on $x+2y+18=0$ and is the only point giving infinitely many solutions; (C) is true.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{R}$ be a relation on $\mathrm{N}\times \mathrm{ℕ}$ defined by $(a,b)\mathrm{R}(c,d)$ if and only if $ad(b-c)=bc(a-d)$. Then $\mathrm{R}$ is
options: symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric
symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $a,b,c,d\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, dividing $ad(b-c)=bc(a-d)$ by $abcd$:

$\frac{1}{c}-\frac{1}{b}=\frac{1}{d}-\frac{1}{a}⟺\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}=\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{d}$

Symmetric: the condition is unchanged when $(a,b)$ and $(c,d)$ are interchanged, so $(a,b)R(c,d)\Rightarrow (c,d)R(a,b)$.

Reflexive: $(a,b)R(a,b)⟺\dfrac{2}{a}=\dfrac{2}{b}⟺a=b$, so for example $(1,2)$ is not related to itself; $R$ is not reflexive.

Transitive: $(2,3)R(3,2)$ since $\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}$, and $(3,2)R(5,30)$ since $\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{5}=\dfrac{8}{15}=\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{30}$. But $\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{5}=\dfrac{21}{30}\neq \dfrac{11}{30}=\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{30}$, so $(2,3)$ is not related to $(5,30)$; $R$ is not transitive.

So $R$ is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\frac{[x]}{1+x^{2}}$, where $[x]$ is greatest integer $\leq x$, is $[2,6)$, then its range is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On each interval $[n,n+1)$, $[x]=n$, and $\dfrac{n}{1+x^{2}}$ decreases for $x>0$, so each piece takes values from its value at the left end (included) down to its limit at the right end (excluded).

$x\in [2,3)$: $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{1+x^{2}}\in \left (\dfrac{1}{5},\dfrac{2}{5}\right ]$

$x\in [3,4)$: $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{1+x^{2}}\in \left (\dfrac{3}{17},\dfrac{3}{10}\right ]$

$x\in [4,5)$: $f(x)=\dfrac{4}{1+x^{2}}\in \left (\dfrac{2}{13},\dfrac{4}{17}\right ]$

$x\in [5,6)$: $f(x)=\dfrac{5}{1+x^{2}}\in \left (\dfrac{5}{37},\dfrac{5}{26}\right ]$

Consecutive pieces overlap: $\dfrac{1}{5}<\dfrac{3}{10}$, $\dfrac{3}{17}<\dfrac{4}{17}$ and $\dfrac{2}{13}<\dfrac{5}{26}$. So the union has no gaps and runs from $\dfrac{5}{37}$ (not attained) to $\dfrac{2}{5}$ (attained at $x=2$); the four points removed in options (A) and (D) all lie inside the first or third piece and are attained.

$\text{Range}=\left (\frac{5}{37},\frac{2}{5}\right ]$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: A wire of length $20\mathrm{m}$ is to be cut into two pieces. A piece of length $l_{1}$ is bent to make a square of area $A_{1}$ and the other piece of length $l_{2}$ is made into a circle of area $A_{2}$. If $2A_{1}+3A_{2}$ is minimum then $(πl_{1}):l_{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\ell _{1}+\ell _{2}=20\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d}\ell _{2}}{\mathrm{d}\ell _{1}}=-1$

$\mathrm{A}_{1}=\left (\frac{\ell _{1}}{4}\right )^{2}$ and $\mathrm{A}_{2}=π\left (\frac{\ell _{2}}{2π}\right )^{2}$

Let $\mathrm{S}=2\mathrm{A}_{1}+3\mathrm{A}_{2}=\frac{\ell _{1}^{2}}{8}+\frac{3\ell _{2}^{2}}{4π}$

$\frac{\mathrm{ds}}{\mathrm{d}\ell _{1}}=0\Rightarrow \frac{2\ell _{1}}{8}+\frac{6\ell _{2}}{4π}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}\ell _{2}}{\mathrm{d}\ell _{1}}=0$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\ell _{1}}{4}=\frac{6\ell _{2}}{4π}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{π\ell _{1}}{\ell _{2}}=6$

text: Let $α\in (0,1)$ and $β=\log _{e}(1-α)$. Let $P_{n}(x)=x+\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{x^{3}}{3}+...+\frac{x^{n}}{n},x\in (0,1)$. Then the integral $\int\limits _{0}^{α}\frac{t^{50}}{1-t}dt$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{α}\frac{t^{50}}{1-t}dt$

$\begin{array}{l} =\int\limits _{0}^{α}\dfrac{t^{50}-1+1}{1-t} \\  \\ =-\int\limits _{0}^{α}\left (\dfrac{1-t^{50}}{1-t}-\dfrac{1}{1-t}\right )dt \\  \\ =-\int\limits _{0}^{α}\left (1+t+\ldots ..+t^{49}\right )+\int\limits _{0}^{α}\dfrac{1}{1-t}dt \end{array}$

$=-\left (\frac{α^{50}}{50}+\frac{α^{49}}{49}+\ldots ..+\frac{α^{1}}{1}\right )+\left (\frac{\ln (1-\mathrm{t})}{-1}\right )_{0}^{α}$ 

$=-\mathrm{P}_{50}(α)-\ln (1-α)$

$=-\mathrm{P}_{50}(α)-β$

solution.body:
$\frac{x-5}{-2}=\frac{y-λ}{0}=\frac{z+λ}{1},λ\geq 0$

text: For all $z\in C$ on the curve $C_{1}:|z|=4$, let the locus of the point $z+\frac{1}{z}$ be the curve $\mathrm{C}_{2}$. Then :

solution.body:
Let $\mathrm{w}=\mathrm{z}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{z}}=4\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}θ}+\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}θ}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{w}=\frac{17}{4}\cos θ+\mathrm{i}\frac{15}{4}\sin θ$

So locus of $w$ is ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{\left (\frac{17}{4}\right )^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{\left (\frac{15}{4}\right )^{2}}=1$

Locus of $\mathrm{z}$ is circle $\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}=16$

So intersect at 4 points.

text: The value of $\int\limits _{\frac{π}{3}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{(2+3\sin x)}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}dx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let I = $\int\limits _{\frac{π}{3}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{(2+3\sin x)}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}dx$

$=\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\frac{2}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}dx+\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\frac{3}{1+\cos x}dx$

$\begin{array}{ll} =\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\dfrac{2(1-\cos x)}{\sin x(1-\cos ^{2}x)} & dx+\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\dfrac{3}{1+\cos x}dx \end{array}$

$=\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\frac{2(1-\cos x)}{\sin ^{3}x}dx+\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\frac{3}{2\cos ^{2}\frac{x}{2}}dx$

$\begin{array}{l} =\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\frac{2}{\sin ^{3}x}dx-\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}2\cot x\mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx+\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\frac{3}{2}\sec ^{2}\frac{x}{2}dx \end{array}$

$=2I_{1}-2I_{2}+\frac{3}{2}I_{3}$

Now, 

$\begin{array}{ll} I_{1} & =\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\mathrm{cosec}^{3}xdx \\  \\ =\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\sqrt{1+\cot ^{2}x}\mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx \end{array}$

Put $\cot x=t\Rightarrow -\mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx=dt$

When, $x=\frac{π}{3}\Rightarrow t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\text{and}x=\frac{π}{2}\Rightarrow t=0$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore  & I_{1}=-\int\limits _{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{0}\sqrt{1+t^{2}}dt \\  \\ = & \int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\sqrt{1+t^{2}}dt \\  \\ = & \left [\dfrac{t}{2}\sqrt{1+t^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{2}\log \left [t+\sqrt{1+t^{2}}\right ]\right ]_{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} \\  \\ = & \dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}\log \sqrt{3} \end{array}$

$I_{2}=\int\limits _{π/3}^{π/2}\cot x\mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx$

Put $\cot x=t\Rightarrow \mathrm{cosec}^{2}xdx=-dt$

When, $x=\frac{π}{3}$
$\Rightarrow t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $x=\frac{π}{2}\Rightarrow t=0$

$\therefore \begin{array}{ll} I_{2} & =-\int\limits _{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{0}tdt \\  \\ =\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}t}tdt=\left [\dfrac{t^{2}}{2}\right ]_{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}=\dfrac{1}{6} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} I_{3}=\int\limits _{\frac{π}{3}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\sec ^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}dx \\  \\ = & 2\left (\tan \dfrac{π}{4}-\tan \dfrac{π}{6}\right )=2\left (1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \quad I=2I_{1}-2I_{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}I_{3} \\  \\ =2\left (\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{2}\log \sqrt{3}\right )-2\left (\dfrac{1}{6}\right )+\dfrac{3}{2}\left (2\left (1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right )\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{2}{3}+\log \sqrt{3}-\dfrac{1}{3}+3-\sqrt{3} \\  \\ =\dfrac{10}{3}-\sqrt{3}+\log _{e}\sqrt{3} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text: Let $α>0$, be the smallest number such that the expansion of $\left (x^{\frac{2}{3}}+\frac{2}{x^{3}}\right )^{30}$ has a term $βx^{-α},β\in \mathrm{ℕ}$. Then $α$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}+1}={}^{30}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}\left (\mathrm{x}^{2/3}\right )^{30-\mathrm{r}}\left (\frac{2}{\mathrm{x}^{3}}\right )^{\mathrm{r}}$

$={}^{30}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}\cdot 2^{\mathrm{r}}\cdot \mathrm{x}^{\frac{60-11\mathrm{r}}{3}}$

$\frac{60-11\mathrm{r}}{3}<0$

$\Rightarrow 11\mathrm{r}>60$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{r}>\frac{60}{11}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=6$

$\mathrm{T}_{7}={}^{30}\mathrm{C}_{6}\cdot 2^{6}\mathrm{x}^{-2}$

We have also observed $β={}^{30}\mathrm{C}_{6}(2)^{6}$ is a natural number.

$\therefore α=2$

text: Number of 4-digit numbers that are less than or equal to 2800 and either divisible by 3 or by 11 , is equal to $____________$.

solution.body:
Numbers which are divisible by 3 (4 digit) and less than or equal to 2800

$=\frac{2799-1002}{3}+1=600$

Numbers which are divisible by 11 (4 digit) and less than or equal to 2800

$=\frac{2794-1001}{11}+1=164$

Numbers which are divisible by 33 (4 digit) and less than or equal to 2800

$=\frac{2772-1023}{33}+1=54$

$\therefore$ Total numbers = $600+164-54=710$

Let $a_{1},a_{2},\ldots ,a_{n}$ be in A.P. If $a_{5}=2a_{7}$ and $a_{11}=18$, then 

$12\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{10}}+\sqrt{a_{11}}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{11}}+\sqrt{a_{12}}}+\ldots +\frac{1}{\sqrt{a_{17}}+\sqrt{a_{18}}}\right )$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$a_{11}=18$

$\begin{array}{l} a+10d=18 \\  \\ a_{5}=2a_{7} \\  \\ a+4d=2(a+6d) \\  \\ a=-8d \end{array}$

(i) and (ii) $\Rightarrow a=-72,d=9$.

On rationalising the denominator, given expression 

$=12\left [\frac{\sqrt{a_{10}}-\sqrt{a_{11}}}{-d}+\frac{\sqrt{a_{11}}-\sqrt{a_{12}}}{-d}+\ldots +\frac{\sqrt{a_{17}}-\sqrt{a_{18}}}{-d}\right ]$ 

$=12\left [\frac{\sqrt{a_{10}}-\sqrt{a_{18}}}{-d}\right ]$

$=12\left [\frac{\sqrt{a_{11}-d}-\sqrt{a_{11}+7d}}{-d}\right ]$

$=12\left [\frac{\sqrt{18-9}-\sqrt{18+63}}{-9}\right ]$ $=12\times \frac{2}{3}=8$

text: Let $⃗{a}$ and $⃗{b}$ be two vectors such that $|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{14},|⃗{b}|=\sqrt{6}$ and $|⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}|=\sqrt{48}$. Then $(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})^{2}$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{14},|⃗{b}|=\sqrt{6}$ and $|⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}|=\sqrt{48}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow |⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}|^{2}+(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})^{2}=|⃗{a}|^{2}|⃗{b}|^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 48+(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})^{2}=6\times 14 \\  \\ \Rightarrow (⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})^{2}=84-48 \\  \\ =36 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift

text:
Let for $x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$,

$f(x)=\frac{x+|x|}{2}\text{and}g(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} x, & x<0 \\ x^{2}, & x\geq 0 \end{array}\text{.} \right.$

Then area bounded by the curve $y=(f\circ g)(x)$ and the lines $y=0,2y-x=15$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\frac{x+|x|}{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x & x\geq 0 \\ 0 & x<0 \end{array} \right.$

$g(x)=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x^{2} & x\geq 0 \\ x & x<0 \end{array} \right.$

$\mathrm{fog}(x)=f[g(x)]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} g(x), & g(x)\geq 0 \\ 0, & g(x)<0 \end{array} \right.$

$\mathrm{fog}(x)=\left [\begin{array}{ll} x^{2}, & x\geq 0 \\ 0, & x<0 \end{array} \right.$

$2y-x=15$


[IMG]


$\mathrm{A}=\int\limits _{0}^{3}\left (\frac{\mathrm{x}+15}{2}-\mathrm{x}^{2}\right )\mathrm{dx}+\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{15}{2}\times 15$

= $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{15x}{2}-\frac{x^{3}}{3}\left |_{0}^{3}+\frac{225}{4} \right.$

$=\frac{9}{4}+\frac{45}{2}-9+\frac{225}{4}=\frac{99-36+225}{4}$

$=\frac{288}{4}=72$

$σ_{\mathrm{x}}^{2}=σ_{\mathrm{d}}^{2}=\frac{\sum \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}}{\sum \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}}-\left (\frac{\sum \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\sum \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{i}}}\right )^{2}$
